newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks seen continuing upward movement.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks seen continuing upward movement.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks are seen moving up in healthy Friday trade and this week's Central Bank report on GDP will have little impact, brokers said.
"There are a number of buyers willing to pay premiums for big quantities of stocks," said Gordon Nadesan of brokerage CT Smith.

Brokers said Wednesday's Central Bank report which said 1996 gross domestic product growth had fallen to 3.8 percent, from 5.5 in 1995, due to a drought and the war in the northeast of the country, would have little impact on the stock market.
"The report held no surprises. Investors who are buying now are looking at future growth, which is seen averaging at over six percent," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena of Ceylinco Stock Brokers.
The market was closed on Thursday for May Day.
Parcels of 3.8 million shares of Kegalle Plantations and 1.55 million Kelani Valley remain on bid at 31.50 rupees and 31 rupees, respectively.
The parcels were introduced on an all-or-none basis on Wednesday in line with stock exchange rules governing the sale of five percent or more of a firm's issued capital.
